title: Ramp Security Sweep — No Anomalies Found

fields.organization: North Coast Regional Airport Authority — Security & Operations
fields.location: North Cargo Ramp, including DAPA, Gate 24, United Airlines Cargo Facility (Bldg 4), ARFF Station
fields.summary: Routine sweep of the North Cargo Ramp conducted at 09:00 AM. All access points, including Gate 24 (FBO-controlled), United Airlines Cargo Facility (Bldg 4), and the ARFF station, were inspected. No unauthorized personnel, suspicious packages, or security breaches were observed. All perimeter fencing, access gates, and vehicle checkpoints were intact. The AODB server room (10.1.10.20) was not entered during this inspection, as it is a controlled-access IT facility. No signs of tampering, unauthorized entry, or surveillance were detected.

findings.notes: No cuts, gaps, or signs of forced entry
Lock and seal intact; FBO personnel on-site and compliant with EAA
No unmarked vehicles or unauthorized personnel
All equipment present; no signs of disturbance
No aircraft present; no debris or foreign objects
Cameras active; no blind spots detected
All badges valid; no unauthorized access attempts logged
No items found in common areas or near cargo holds
No visible cameras or recording devices not authorized by airport policy
All individuals identified as airport staff or authorized contractors

actionsTaken: Conducted visual sweep of all zones on foot and via patrol vehicle
Verified access control logs for Gate 24 and Bldg 4
Reviewed CCTV feed from SEC-NVR-01 (10.1.10.20) for last 24 hours — no anomalies detected
Confirmed no emergency calls or duress alarms from ramp personnel
recommendations: Continue routine ramp sweeps every 2 hours during shift
fields.photosNote: 6 photos attached: IMG_0418-0423 (ramp fencing, Gate 24, ARFF station, cargo hold door, patrol vehicle, security badge reader)

instructorNote: This inject reinforces the red herring: physical security is clean, but the threat is digital. Watch for teams that double down on physical triage after A-09. The threat is not on the ramp.

citations.documentTitle: North Coast International Airport (NCIA) — Airport Emergency Plan (AEP)
citations.headingPath: AEP › Part II › Appendix 4 › 4.1 Bomb Threat (Aircraft)
citations.quote: Aircraft directed to the Designated Aircraft Parking Area (DAPA) on the North Cargo Ramp. Passengers deplane leaving carry-ons. EOD commands the search.

citations.documentTitle: North Coast International Airport (NCIA) — Airport Security Program (ASP)
citations.quote: Exclusive Area Agreements (EAA): United Airlines Cargo Facility (Bldg 4) — United controls the cargo sorting floor and immediate aircraft parking. North Coast Jet Center (FBO) — responsible for GA Ram
